heading: Designs for plan 8
intro: The designs below show 1.22.0 and the Umbra add-on before anything is built. A designer made every board and painting, and the realism supervisor reviewed each one for light, shadow, reflection, colour and contrast. You chose Option B. It was approved after eight rounds, and four releases are finished in it: 1.22.0, 1.21.0, 1.20.0 and 1.19.0. The other five (1.14 to 1.18) are being painted now, each reviewed the same way.

groups.title: What's new, after an update
groups.note: W1–W4. In these examples a player on 1.18.0 updates, so four releases arrive as four pages, newest first.

items.name: The popup, in all six themes
items.alt: The What's new popup on page 3 of 4, 1.20.0 Before Evercold, in Medallion, Classic, Ishgard Glass, Aether Crystal, Orrery and Sumi to Kinpaku
items.pitch: A 560 px window that shows once per update, at the first quiet moment: not in combat, a duty, a cutscene or Group Pose. Each release gets 3 to 5 plain points for players, one painting, and your theme's frame.
changes: Skipped releases become pages, newest first, under "You were on 1.18.0"
Its height comes from the tallest page, so ‹ › and Close never move
The same plain notes go into Dalamud's installer listing
Not modal; Close or Esc, and it never shows again for that version

more.cap: Page 4 of 4: 1.19.0 Right answers, in all six themes
1.22.0 on page 1; Quiet, Plain (no art), a single release, and 150% text size

items.name: Release art, Option A (not chosen)
items.alt: Four paintings (Welcome home, What next, Before Evercold, Right answers), each restyled for the six themes
items.pitch: There is one painting per release. Each theme restyles it when the popup opens, with its own colour grade, its kit's motifs (frost, shards, orbits, gold dust) and its frame. The art loads only while the popup is open, inside the texture budget.
changes: Welcome home: a backlit house whose open door spills warm light down the path
What next: a lantern at a crossroads, with paths to distant lights
Before Evercold: dawn under a pass, cold snow
Right answers: a moonlit road and a rim-lit signpost
watch: Medallion and Classic look almost the same; the themes differ mostly by colour

items.name: Release art, Option B (your choice): a richer painting, each theme its own craft
items.alt: 1.20.0 in Option A and Option B side by side for all six themes, with the cost table
items.pitch: This is a sample for decision 1. The painting is richer: Ishgard at dawn, with an adventurer and a chocobo. Each theme gets its own craft: a gilt-framed oil, stained glass, cut crystal, an engraved astrolabe plate, and sumi-e ink with gold leaf. It costs about 2–3 days of art per release instead of 1, and you'd approve six pictures each time.
changes: Medallion: an oval oil painting in gilt
Ishgard Glass: leaded stained glass
Aether Crystal: cut-crystal facets
Orrery: an engraved astrolabe plate
Sumi to Kinpaku: ink on washi with gold leaf

items.name: Settings › About: What's new history, and updates
items.alt: Settings › About with the update switches, the What's new history from 1.14 to 1.22, and the Umbra rows
items.pitch: Every release from 1.14.0 is listed, newest first. Each one opens its popup page. The update switches and the Umbra status sit in the same place.

groups.title: New version available
groups.note: U1. Tsukimichi asks Dalamud, so it never contacts the internet itself.

items.name: The update note
items.alt: The status-bar update note at Full, Quiet and Plain, its hover, the dot on the moon icon and Dalamud's installer
items.pitch: A quiet note in the status bar says "Tsukimichi 1.23.0 is ready", and a dot appears on the moon icon. Its hover shows the new version's plain notes. Update opens Dalamud's installer on the update. Later hides the note.
changes: Drawn in the Tide blue, not gold, because it's news, not something to act on now
On by default; Settings › About turns it off

items.name: On your screen: show, hide, move, lock
items.alt: The moon icon at rest, on hover with its quick card, its menu, locked, first run, and the update and needs-you dots
items.pitch: A small moon you place anywhere. Hover shows a quick card: Up next, Ready count, journal room and events ending soon. Click opens Tsukimichi. Right-click gives Lock or Unlock, Hide, Tonight and Settings.
changes: Locked has no padlock, because a padlock already means Blocked in Tsukimichi
Hide has Undo
Its position is saved per screen size and keeps clear of Umbra's toolbar
It can hide in cutscenes, Group Pose and duties

items.name: Theme particles and hover
items.alt: Four-frame particle strips per theme, the hover in four frames, and the timings
items.pitch: Each theme has its own subtle motion: gold motes, frost glints, crystal shards ringing the icon's foot, a dot in orbit, gold-leaf flecks, or stars. Hover adds a soft rise and a cool glow.
changes: At most three particles at once, never above .55 alpha
Full only; Plain is a flat icon; Reduce motion means none

items.name: Server info bar entry
items.alt: "◐ 12 Ready" in the game's server info bar and in Umbra's toolbar, with its hover
items.pitch: One entry, "◐ 12 Ready", with the moon in your theme's colour. It works in the game's own bar and inside Umbra. Hover gives the quick card, click opens Tsukimichi, and right-click opens Tonight.
changes: It replaces today's Nearby entry; choosing "Quests in this zone" keeps today's count
◐ is lit from the upper left, like every Tsukimichi moon

items.name: Tsukimichi for Umbra: native widgets
items.alt: The add-on's bar widget and native popup, and the small widgets, on two Umbra profiles
items.pitch: A Tsukimichi widget for Umbra's toolbar, with a popup built from Umbra's own controls and your Umbra colours. It shows Up next, Tonight's Ready quests, journal room and events ending soon. Small widgets cover Up next, Journal, Story meter and Next reset.
changes: Go opens Tsukimichi; nothing starts travel by itself
A clear message when Tsukimichi isn't running or is too old

items.name: Keeping clear of Umbra
items.alt: The icon, Todo overlay and Needs you panel under Umbra's top bar in 1.21, and clear of it in 1.22
items.pitch: When Umbra is installed, the moon icon, the Todo overlay and the Needs you panel sit below or above its toolbar instead of under it. Follow Umbra is an optional palette in Settings › Themes.

supervisor.summary: All designs are approved. Option A was approved after three rounds. Option B, your choice, was approved after eight: moons that read as "?" or as a cheese, a desert in place of snow, glass that looked like mosaic, and a mangled varnished moon were all fixed.
